content:
Apple's existing iPad, the A16 model, hasn't been updated in over a year. It remains the only device in Apple's core product line that doesn't support Apple Intelligence. Rumors about an A18 model launching this year have been circulating for a while. Now, it seems Apple has bigger plans.

It's reasonable to speculate that this product delay is largely related to the memory crisis plaguing the electronics industry. If Apple had originally scheduled the A18 refresh for earlier this year to launch alongside the M4 iPad Air, and then was forced to delay it, I wouldn't be surprised at all.

A reminder: Apple raised the base iPad's price from US$349 to US$449 this summer, alongside other products that saw price hikes due to memory issues. This price is actually the same as when it first launched in 2022.

New iPad Details

However, MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris dropped some more exciting news. The next base-model iPad doesn't appear to use an A18 chip, but rather comes equipped with an A19 chip. In addition to the A19 chip, it'll also feature the N1 networking chip, and a C1X modem for the cellular version. This means Apple's most affordable iPad will support Wi-Fi 7.

The A19 iPad will also come with 8GB of RAM, allowing users to access Siri's AI features, though you still won't get the most powerful on-device models or the more advanced voice dictation models, as those require 12GB of RAM. It's not a major loss, but worth mentioning.

Another possibility is that the A19 iPad might get a new name. With the launch of the MacBook Neo, Apple's marketing chief Greg Joswiak pointed out that simply calling the MacBook Neo a "MacBook" would strip it of its unique identity. Hopefully the next base-model iPad will also get a more proper name, like "SE" or "Neo" or something, so we have something to call it.

Beyond that, don't expect any redesign or display upgrades. There might be new colors, but probably nothing else. Personally, I hope Apple will add USB 3 to this model so users don't have to suffer those painfully slow transfer speeds anymore. At least that would help justify the new higher price tag.

Release Date

Top comment from MaxM

The iPad really... I hope they can bump up the display refresh rates. Base—90Hz, Air—120Hz, Pro—144Hz or higher. Something like that. As for the chip, I always say this, but tablet chips have always been top-tier, so even now they're still more than capable.

According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple's next affordable iPad should launch next spring, alongside other products including the M6 MacBook Air, A19 Pro MacBook Neo, M7 14-inch MacBook Pro, and more.

Are you planning to buy the base-model iPad? What are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments.
